report.tagline: India's free public digital rails: Aadhaar proves who you are, DigiLocker holds your official documents, and UPI moves money instantly.
report.simpleSummary: The government built a few free building blocks that any app can plug into. Aadhaar lets you prove your identity with a number and an OTP. DigiLocker keeps real copies of your marksheets, licence and PAN card on your phone. UPI lets you send money to anyone in seconds for free, and apps like PhonePe and Google Pay are built on top of it.

overview.whatItDoes: India Stack is a set of public digital systems built by the government and non-profit bodies. Aadhaar (by UIDAI) gives each resident a digital ID. DigiLocker (by MeitY) stores official documents issued straight from the source, like CBSE or the transport department. UPI (by NPCI) lets any bank account send money to any other, through any app. Private companies build products on top for free or very low cost.
howItWorks: Aadhaar: you share your number, get an OTP on your phone, and the app confirms who you are (eKYC).
DigiLocker: issuers like CBSE, RTO and Income Tax push your documents into your locker. They count as originals by law.
Requesters like banks and telecom firms can pull a verified document with your consent instead of asking for a photocopy.
UPI: you link your bank to an app and get an ID like name@bank. Money moves bank to bank in seconds.
Apps like PhonePe, Google Pay and Paytm are only front ends; NPCI runs the switch in the middle.
Most of these services are free to citizens, and UPI is free for most payments to merchants too.
overview.valueProposition: For citizens: no queues, no photocopies, free instant payments. For companies: they can verify customers and collect money cheaply, so they can build products for crores of people that would cost too much otherwise.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Confirms a person's identity using their Aadhaar number and OTP or fingerprint.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Cut the cost of onboarding a bank or telecom customer from hundreds of rupees to a few rupees.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Stores marksheets, driving licence, PAN, vehicle RC and more, issued directly by the source.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Legally valid originals reduce fraud and paperwork.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Lets banks, colleges and employers fetch a document with the user's permission.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Private apps can verify users without asking for uploads.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Instant bank-to-bank payments through any app using a UPI ID or QR code.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Made digital payments normal for crores of small merchants.

coreFeatures.feature: UPI AutoPay and credit on UPI
coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Auto-debits for subscriptions and EMIs; RuPay credit cards and credit lines can be used on UPI.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Opens lending and subscription businesses on the same rails.

businessModel.summary: These are public goods, not businesses. They are funded mostly by the government and banks. The point is to make it cheap for private companies to build products, so the money is made by apps built on top, not by the rails.

revenueStreams.detail: UIDAI and MeitY budgets pay for Aadhaar and DigiLocker.
Private companies pay small per-check fees for Aadhaar eKYC and some DigiLocker pulls.
The government pays banks an incentive for small UPI payments since merchants pay zero fee.

revenueStreams.stream: Planned UPI MDR on large payments
revenueStreams.detail: A 0.4% fee (capped at ₹300) on some merchant payments above ₹2,000, and ₹5 flat in categories like fuel and telecom, was due 15 October 2026 but pushed to after Diwali. Over 95% of merchant payments stay free.

businessModel.pricing: Free for citizens. UPI is free for person-to-person and most merchant payments. Aadhaar eKYC costs a few rupees per check for private companies. DigiLocker partner pricing is not widely published.
costDrivers: Data centres and security for crores of daily requests
Onboarding new document issuers across states
businessModel.unitEconomics: Look at one ₹200 UPI payment at a kirana shop. The customer pays nothing and the shop pays nothing. The banks and NPCI spend a fraction of a rupee to process it, partly covered by a government incentive. With a card, the shop would have paid about ₹2 to ₹4. For a fintech, Aadhaar eKYC costs a few rupees per user, against ₹100+ for a paper KYC visit. The rails lose or break even so that the whole economy saves. Per-transaction costs here are estimates.

growth.moat: They are open and run by the state, so everyone builds on them. Every bank, app and shop is already connected, and laws recognise DigiLocker documents as originals. No private company can match that reach or legal standing.

pmLessons: Open public rails let private companies compete on experience. PhonePe and Google Pay won by building on free UPI.
Making the base layer free can grow a whole market, but someone must pay. UPI's MDR debate shows this.
Trust can come from the source. DigiLocker works because documents come from the issuer.
Before building a feature, check if a public rail already solves it. Many Indian startups exist because eKYC and UPI made onboarding cheap.
Design for the weakest user too. Fingerprint failures show that average success rates hide real pain.

interviewQuestions.question: UPI is free. How should it be funded?
interviewQuestions.hint: List who benefits (merchants, apps, government). Compare options: subsidy, MDR on large merchants, value-added services. Protect small merchants.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you increase DigiLocker usage among private companies?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find why they don't use it (coverage, API ease, cost). Propose a simple SDK, more issuers and clear pricing. Track requester count and fetches.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a feature to cut UPI fraud for first-time users.
interviewQuestions.hint: Map the scam flow, add friction only at risky moments, use plain-language warnings, and measure fraud and drop-off.

interviewQuestions.question: Why did UPI beat wallets in India?
interviewQuestions.hint: Interoperability, zero cost, bank account link, no loading money, and government push.

interviewQuestions.question: You are a PM at a lending startup. Which India Stack parts would you use and why?
interviewQuestions.hint: Aadhaar eKYC to onboard, DigiLocker for PAN and income proof, UPI AutoPay for EMIs, Account Aggregator for bank data.

glossary.meaning: The set of public digital systems in India, such as Aadhaar, DigiLocker and UPI, that anyone can build on.
Electronic know-your-customer: verifying a person's identity online instead of on paper.
Merchant discount rate: the fee a shop pays for accepting a digital payment.
Different apps and banks working with each other.
National Payments Corporation of India, the body that runs UPI.
Person to merchant: a payment from a customer to a shop.
The one number that best shows the value a product gives its users.
Something built for everyone to use, usually funded by the government.
